rounds.response:
Q: When can we extend a trial? A: The standard trial is 14 days; agents may grant extensions for legitimate business reasons (implementation delays, procurement review, integration testing) up to a 60-day total trial period across CoreSupport and EnterpriseShield—always record the customer's reason and the new end date in the ticket.  
Key conditions/limits: extensions require a documented "good reason," you must track cumulative days to avoid exceeding the ~60-day cap, and this practice applies to our main products (note legacy/beta plans may differ).  
Escalate instead of extending when the customer requests >60 days, ties the extension to pricing/discount negotiations, requires commercial approval, or you suspect abuse/fraud; if unsure, check the trial policy KB or ask your supervisor before granting.

rounds.response:
Q: What if the customer asks for a trial extension after their trial has already expired? A: If granting/restarting the trial would keep the total trial time within the ~60‑day cap and the customer provides a legitimate business reason, agents may restart or extend the trial and must record the reason and the new end date in the ticket.  
Allowed actions: restart the trial window or add remaining allowable days up to the ~60‑day total (applies to CoreSupport and EnterpriseShield); always track cumulative days and note the justification.  
Escalate instead of granting when the account appears suspicious, the customer requests >60 days, the ask is tied to pricing/discounts or commercial approval, or the KB prescribes a different flow.  
If the internal trial policy conflicts with this guidance, follow the KB/escalation matrix and flag the discrepancy for your supervisor.
